scope.linux_additional_scope: Qt Wayland and Linux platform integrations, including conditional D-Bus and XCB dependencies.
scope.selection: Upstream qt_attribution.json records from the listed source packages and their referenced license and copyright files; applicable LICENSES texts; LGPLv3 and its GPLv3 text; WebP patent grant. Retained notices can cover optional runtime implementations; this inventory does not assert that every implementation is bundled.

excluded_records.android-native-style: Android platform is outside the Windows/Linux scope.
excluded_records.android-gradle-wrapper: Android packaging build tool is outside the runtime scope.
excluded_records.sqlite: QtSql is not in the identified collected modules.
excluded_records.dejayvu: WebAssembly platform is outside the Windows/Linux scope.
excluded_records.qeventdispatcher_cf: macOS platform is outside the Windows/Linux scope.
excluded_records.cocoa-platform-plugin: macOS platform is outside the Windows/Linux scope.
excluded_records.yoga: QtQuick.Layouts is not in the identified collected modules.
excluded_records.shadow_angular_material: QtQuickControls is not in the identified collected modules.
excluded_records.pixman: ARM NEON code is outside the locked x86-64 platform scope.

boundaries: QtGui's PDF generation attribution remains relevant independently of the excluded QtPdf image plugin.
Upstream Wayland records can name qtwaylandcompositor while also describing platform-plugin use; retaining their texts does not assert that a compositor library is distributed.
PySide's designated Python license file bufferprocs_py37.h is retained in full because the upstream attribution points to that header.
The Python-2.0 attribution uses its referenced PSF-3.7.0.txt; the PySide source archive has no LICENSES/Python-2.0.txt.
License alternatives are preserved without selecting a legal route.
